topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks introduce the lecture topic on cancer therapy and outline the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies, toxicities, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss local interventions and traditional cytotoxic chemotherapies along with their systemic toxicities and mechanisms of drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and genetic defects in cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain strategies to selectively kill cancer cells by exploiting specific vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, resistance mechanisms, and drug addiction
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the targeting of hyperactive oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and examine the molecular mechanisms driving drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Targeted monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches utilizing engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to direct cytotoxic effects to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune targeting
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine natural immune surveillance and therapeutic methods that harness or engineer T cells, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Clinical progress, challenges, and future perspectives in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the overall clinical progress, persistent challenges in therapy design, and future strategies for cancer detection, prevention, and treatment combinations.
